questions.q: Why does the backup script set `pipefail` before running `pg_dump | gzip`?
options: pipefail makes gzip compress files more tightly
Without it, a failing pg_dump in the middle of the pipe can be masked by gzip succeeding on empty input, so the script would report success on an empty backup
pipefail is required for any script that uses a pipe, regardless of behavior
It speeds up the pg_dump command
questions.explain: By default, a pipeline's exit status is only the last command's. pipefail makes the whole pipeline fail if any command in it fails, so a broken pg_dump doesn't get hidden behind gzip's own success.

questions.q: Why does the lesson upload the backup to S3 instead of only keeping it in /var/backups on the server?
options: Local backups take up no disk space, so S3 is purely optional
A backup that only exists on the server it protects is lost if that server itself is lost -- S3 keeps a copy that survives the server
S3 uploads are always faster than local disk writes
pg_dump cannot write directly to a local file
questions.explain: If the only copy of a backup lives on the same server being backed up, losing that server means losing the backup along with it. Shipping a copy to S3 protects against that single point of failure.

questions.q: What does the local retention-policy loop use to decide whether a backup file should be deleted?
options: The file's name length
Whether the file's last-modified time (st_mtime) is older than the retention cutoff
Whether the file is larger than 1 GB
The number of times the file has been downloaded
questions.explain: The script reads each backup's last-modified timestamp with .stat().st_mtime and compares it against a cutoff date; anything modified before the cutoff gets deleted with .unlink().

questions.q: Why does the S3 cleanup step use a paginator instead of a single list_objects_v2 call?
options: Paginators are required for all S3 calls regardless of result size
A bucket of nightly backups accumulated over time will eventually exceed what a single list_objects_v2 call returns, the same reason lesson 16 used one for S3 cleanup
Paginators delete objects automatically without any code
list_objects_v2 cannot filter by prefix
questions.explain: Like the earlier cloud-cleanup lesson, a growing bucket of nightly backups will eventually span more results than one list_objects_v2 call returns, so a paginator is used to walk every page safely.

questions.q: Why should a backup script exit with a non-zero status on failure instead of printing an error and continuing?
options: Non-zero exit codes make the script run faster
A non-zero exit code is what lets monitoring or a scheduler actually detect the failure, instead of a backup silently failing with nobody noticing
Exit codes have no effect on anything outside the script itself
It is only a stylistic preference with no functional effect
questions.explain: A script that logs an error but still exits 0 looks successful to anything checking its exit status -- cron, monitoring, a CI pipeline. Exiting non-zero on failure is what makes the failure visible to those systems.
